require "csv"

# Returns up to +count+ CSV::Row objects with the highest numeric values in
# +column+. +column+ may be a header name or a zero-based column index.
# Rows with non-numeric values in that column are ranked last.
def top_rows(file_path, column, count = 5)
  rows = CSV.read(file_path, headers: true)
  return [] if rows.headers.nil?

  validate_column!(rows.headers, column)

  rows.each_with_index
      .sort_by { |row, index| [-numeric_value(row[column]), index] }
      .first(count)
      .map(&:first)
end

private

def validate_column!(headers, column)
  if column.is_a?(Integer)
    return if column >= 0 && column < headers.length
  elsif headers.include?(column)
    return
  end

  raise ArgumentError, "unknown column: #{column.inspect}"
end

def numeric_value(value)
  Float(value)
rescue ArgumentError, TypeError
  -Float::INFINITY
end
